source.text: καὶ βαστάζων αὑτῷ τὸν σταυρὸν ἐξῆλθεν εἰς τὸν λεγόμενον Κρανίου Τόπον, ὃ λέγεται Ἑβραϊστὶ Γολγοθα, ὅπου αὐτὸν ἐσταύρωσαν, καὶ μετ’ αὐτοῦ ἄλλους δύο ἐντεῦθεν καὶ ἐντεῦθεν, μέσον δὲ τὸν Ἰησοῦν.

records.literal_gloss: And carrying for himself the cross he went out to the [place] being called Of-a-Skull Place, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha, \v 18 where him they crucified, and with him others two, on this side and on that side, and in the middle the Jesus.

en.L: And carrying the cross by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to the [place] called Place of a Skull, which is called in Hebrew Golgotha, \v 18 where they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} two others, on this side and on that side, and Jesus in the middle.
en.B: Carrying the cross by {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out to what is called the Place of the Skull (in Hebrew, Golgotha). \v 18 There they crucified {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, along with two others, one on each side and Jesus in the middle.
en.R: Jesus carried {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own cross and went out of the city to a place called Skull Place. In the Hebrew language its name is Golgotha. \v 18 There the soldiers nailed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to the cross. They also crucified two other men, one on each side of Jesus, so that Jesus was in the middle.

es.L: Y cargando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo la cruz, salió al llamado Lugar de la Calavera, que en hebreo se dice Gólgota, \v 18 donde {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucificaron, y con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a otros dos, de un lado y de otro, y en medio a Jesús.
es.B: Cargando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo la cruz, salió hacia el lugar que llaman Lugar de la Calavera (en hebreo, Gólgota). \v 18 Allí {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} crucificaron, y también a otros dos, uno de cada lado, con Jesús en el centro.
es.R: Jesús cargó {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} propia cruz y salió de la ciudad hacia un lugar llamado la Calavera. En idioma hebreo se llama Gólgota. \v 18 Allí los soldados {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} clavaron en la cruz. También crucificaron a otros dos hombres, uno a cada lado de Jesús. Así Jesús quedó en medio.

fr.L: Et portant la croix {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}}, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit vers le [lieu] appelé Lieu du Crâne, qui se dit en hébreu Golgotha, \v 18 où ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifièrent, et avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} deux autres, de part et d’autre, et Jésus au milieu.
fr.B: Portant {{deity_pronoun:lui-même|Lui-même}} la croix, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} sortit vers ce qu’on appelle le Lieu du Crâne (en hébreu, Golgotha). \v 18 Là, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} crucifièrent, ainsi que deux autres, un de chaque côté, et Jésus au milieu.
fr.R: Jésus a porté {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} propre croix et il est sorti de la ville vers un endroit appelé le Lieu du Crâne. En hébreu, on l’appelait Golgotha. \v 18 Là, les soldats {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont cloué sur la croix. Ils ont aussi crucifié deux autres hommes, un de chaque côté de Jésus. Jésus était donc au milieu.

sw.L: Na akiubeba msalaba {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, alitoka kwenda mahali palipoitwa Mahali pa Fuvu, ambapo kwa Kiebrania panaitwa Golgotha, \v 18 ambapo walimsulubisha, na pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} wengine wawili, huku na huku, na Yesu katikati.
sw.B: Akiubeba msalaba {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}, alitoka kwenda mahali panapoitwa Mahali pa Fuvu (kwa Kiebrania, Golgotha). \v 18 Huko walimsulubisha pamoja na wengine wawili, mmoja kila upande, na Yesu katikati.
sw.R: Yesu aliubeba msalaba {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} mwenyewe, akatoka nje ya mji kwenda mahali palipoitwa Mahali pa Fuvu. Kwa lugha ya Kiebrania jina lake ni Golgotha. \v 18 Huko askari walimpigilia misumari msalabani. Pia waliwasulubisha watu wengine wawili, mmoja kila upande wa Yesu, hivyo Yesu alikuwa katikati.

vi.L: Và tự mình vác cây thập tự, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra đến chỗ gọi là Nơi Cái Sọ, tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ gọi là Gô-gô-tha, \v 18 là nơi họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, và cùng với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} hai người khác, bên này một người, bên kia một người, còn Đức Giê-xu ở giữa.
vi.B: Tự mình vác cây thập tự, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đi ra đến nơi gọi là Nơi Cái Sọ (tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ là Gô-gô-tha). \v 18 Tại đó họ đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cùng với hai người khác, mỗi bên một người, còn Đức Giê-xu ở giữa.
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu tự vác cây thập tự của mình ra khỏi thành, đến một nơi gọi là Cái Sọ. Trong tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ, nơi ấy gọi là Gô-gô-tha. \v 18 Tại đó, những người lính đóng đinh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên cây thập tự. Họ cũng đóng đinh hai người khác, mỗi người một bên, còn Đức Giê-xu ở giữa.

ko.L: 그리고 그분은 스스로 십자가를 지시고, 해골의 곳이라고 불리는 [곳], 히브리 말로는 골고다라고 하는 곳으로 나가셨다. \v 18 거기서 그들이 그분을 십자가에 못 박았고, 그분과 함께 다른 두 사람도 이쪽과 저쪽에 [못 박고], 예수를 가운데에 [두었다].
ko.B: 예수께서는 몸소 십자가를 지고, 해골 터라고 하는 곳으로 나가셨다. 그곳은 히브리 말로 골고다라고 한다. \v 18 거기서 그들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박았다. 다른 두 사람도 함께 못 박았는데, 양쪽에 한 사람씩 두고 예수를 가운데에 두었다.
ko.R: 예수께서는 자신의 십자가를 직접 지고 성 밖으로 나가셨다. 그리고 해골 터라는 곳에 이르셨다. 그곳은 히브리 말로 골고다라고 했다. \v 18 거기서 병사들이 예수를 십자가에 못 박았다. 다른 두 사람도 예수의 양쪽에 하나씩 십자가에 못 박았다. 그래서 예수께서는 가운데에 계셨다.

pt.L: E, carregando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} mesmo a cruz, saiu para o [lugar] chamado Lugar da Caveira, que em hebraico se chama Gólgota, \v 18 onde {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} crucificaram, e com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} outros dois, um de cada lado, e Jesus no meio.
pt.B: Carregando {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} mesmo a cruz, saiu para o lugar chamado Lugar da Caveira (em hebraico, Gólgota). \v 18 Ali {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} crucificaram, e com {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} outros dois, um de cada lado, e Jesus no meio.
pt.R: Jesus carregou a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} própria cruz e saiu da cidade para um lugar chamado Lugar da Caveira. Na língua hebraica, o nome desse lugar é Gólgota. \v 18 Ali os soldados {{deity_pronoun:o|O}} pregaram na cruz. Eles também crucificaram outros dois homens, um de cada lado de Jesus. Assim, Jesus ficou no meio.

decisions.choice: carrying the cross by himself, with no one's help
alternatives: carrying the cross for his own sake
only that he set out carrying it, leaving open whether someone helped later
decisions.reason: The small word attached to "carrying" points back to Jesus: the cross was his own load. Matthew, Mark and Luke say the soldiers made Simon of Cyrene carry it (Matthew 27:32; Mark 15:21; Luke 23:26). John does not mention Simon. The accounts can be read together (Jesus set out carrying it and Simon took it over on the way), but John's own telling shows Jesus carrying it himself.

decisions.choice: the cross: probably the crossbeam, which a condemned man carried to the place of execution
alternatives: the whole cross, upright and crossbeam
decisions.reason: Roman practice was for the condemned person to carry his cross to the place of execution, where the upright post often stood ready. What he carried was most likely the crossbeam, since a whole cross would have been too heavy for one man, especially one who had been flogged (19:1). John only says "the cross".

decisions.choice: Place of a Skull, in the local language Golgotha: John translates the name for his readers
decisions.reason: John gives the meaning of the name before the local name itself. "Hebrew" is John's word for the language of the Jews of the land, which in daily speech was mostly Aramaic, and Golgotha is the Aramaic word for "skull" (see 5:2; 19:13). Why it had that name is not known; it may have been the shape of the ground. The place was outside the city but near it (19:20; Hebrews 13:12).

decisions.choice: they crucified him: the Roman soldiers, as 19:23 says; and two others, whom John does not name
decisions.reason: The verb has no stated subject, and 19:16 says Pilate handed Jesus over "to them". But 19:23 says plainly that the soldiers crucified Jesus: crucifixion was a Roman penalty, carried out by Roman soldiers on the governor's order. John does not say who the other two men were; the other Gospels call them bandits or criminals (Mark 15:27; Luke 23:32-33).

decisions.choice: the soldiers nailed him to the cross (R)
decisions.reason: Readable names the soldiers, from 19:23 (meaning decision m4), so that young readers do not take "they" to mean the last group mentioned. "Nailed" comes from the nail marks in 20:25 and explains the word "crucified" for readers who may not know it.

decisions.choice: Place of a Skull (L); the Place of the Skull (B); Skull Place (R); in Hebrew (every level)
decisions.reason: Each level gives John's own translation of the name. "Calvary" comes from the Latin word for skull and is not in the Greek. "Hebrew" keeps the word John used; meaning decision m3 explains which language this was.

decisions.choice: past tense (pretérito); Literal keeps the present where John uses it (verses 26, 27, 28)
decisions.reason: As in English: John often tells his story in the present tense ("dice"). Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable use the past, as Spanish stories are told. This applies to every such verb in the passage.

decisions.choice: Lugar de la Calavera (L, B); la Calavera (R); en hebreo Gólgota
decisions.reason: Each level gives John's own translation of the name. "Calavera" is the Spanish word for a skull; "Calvario" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek. "En hebreo" keeps John's word (meaning decision m3), as at 5:2 and 19:13.

decisions.choice: los soldados lo clavaron en la cruz (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names the soldiers, from 19:23 (meaning decision m4), and "clavaron" comes from the nail marks of 20:25 and explains "crucificar" for readers who may not know it.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo; con {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; and every other pronoun for Christ
decisions.reason: By the book-wide rule (1:1), every pronoun for Christ takes the deity_pronoun setting: stressed (él), possessive (su, sus, mi, mis) and object pronouns before the verb (lo, le, and "se" for "le" in "se la acercaron"). Pronouns for his mother, the disciple and the soldiers take no setting.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B), with Literal keeping John's present tense ("il dit" in 19:26, 27, 28); passé composé (R); speech in the passé composé at every level
decisions.reason: The French brief for the passage (19:17-30). The passé simple ("sortit", "crucifièrent") is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Literal uses it for the Greek past tenses and keeps the present where John tells a past event in the present, as the English Literal does. Readable uses the passé composé ("Jésus a porté"), the past tense French readers speak and learn first; the imperfect is used at every level for what was going on.

decisions.choice: le Lieu du Crâne, en hébreu Golgotha (every level); les soldats l'ont cloué sur la croix (R)
decisions.reason: Each level gives John's own translation of the name, with capitals as a place name. "Calvaire" comes from the Latin word for skull and is not in the Greek. Readable names the soldiers, from 19:23, and says "cloué" to explain the word "crucifié", as the English Readable does (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: historic present kept at Literal ("anasema", "anamwambia", 19:26-28); narrative past at Balanced and Readable, -li- for the first verb of a sequence and -ka- for those that follow
decisions.reason: John tells parts of this scene in the present ("he says"). Literal keeps it, as the English Literal does; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past, as written Swahili narrative does. Swahili carries most pronouns inside the verb, where no capital can be shown, so the deity_pronoun setting appears only on free pronouns and possessives ("mwenyewe", "naye", "yake"). This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: Mahali pa Fuvu ... kwa Kiebrania Golgotha (every level)
decisions.reason: John translates the name for his readers (meaning decision m3), so each level gives the meaning, "Mahali pa Fuvu" (the place of a skull), then the local name. "Kalvari" comes from the Latin and is not in the Greek. "Kwa Kiebrania" keeps the word John used, as at 19:13.

decisions.choice: "cây thập tự"
decisions.reason: "cây thập tự" is the plain Protestant word, used through this passage; "thập giá" is the Catholic one (style guide section 4).

decisions.choice: "Nơi Cái Sọ" (L, B); "Cái Sọ" (R)
decisions.reason: "Đồi Sọ" is familiar but adds a hill that John does not mention. The name is translated literally and capitalised.

decisions.choice: "해골의 곳" (L); "해골 터" (B, R); "골고다" and "히브리 말" at every level
decisions.reason: John translates the place name for his readers; Korean gives the meaning and then the name in its established Protestant form. "터" is a plain word for a site and avoids the wording of older versions.

decisions.choice: No deity_pronoun spans in Korean; the narrator uses "예수께서", "그분" and the honorific -시- for Jesus
alternatives: capitalised pronoun spans as in English
decisions.reason: Korean has no capital letters, so the setting has nothing to change (style guide, section 7). Recorded once for this passage.

decisions.choice: Lugar da Caveira; Gólgota
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 27:33: Portuguese gives John's own translation of the name as "Lugar da Caveira" and spells the Aramaic name as Portuguese writes its sounds, "Gólgota". "Calvário" comes from the Latin and is not what John wrote.

source.text: ἔγραψεν δὲ καὶ τίτλον ὁ Πιλᾶτος καὶ ἔθηκεν ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ· ἦν δὲ γεγραμμένον· Ἰησοῦς ὁ Ναζωραῖος ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

records.literal_gloss: Wrote and also a title the Pilate and put [it] on the cross; was and written: Jesus the Nazorean the king of the Jews.

en.L: And Pilate also wrote a notice and put [it] on the cross; and it was written: "Jesus the Nazorean, the King of the Jews."
en.B: Pilate also wrote a notice and had it placed on the cross. The wording was: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews."
en.R: Pilate also wrote a sign and had it put on the cross. It said, "Jesus from Nazareth, the King of the Jews."

es.L: Escribió también Pilato un letrero y [lo] puso sobre la cruz; y estaba escrito: «Jesús el Nazoreo, el Rey de los judíos».
es.B: Pilato también escribió un letrero y lo hizo poner sobre la cruz. Decía: «Jesús de Nazaret, el Rey de los judíos».
es.R: Pilato también escribió un cartel y lo hizo poner en la cruz. Decía: «Jesús de Nazaret, el Rey de los judíos».

fr.L: Et Pilate écrivit aussi un écriteau et [le] plaça sur la croix ; et il y était écrit : « Jésus le Nazôréen, le roi des Juifs. »
fr.B: Pilate écrivit aussi un écriteau et le fit placer sur la croix. On y lisait : « Jésus de Nazareth, le roi des Juifs. »
fr.R: Pilate a aussi écrit une pancarte et l’a fait mettre sur la croix. On pouvait y lire : « Jésus de Nazareth, le roi des Juifs. »

sw.L: Na Pilato aliandika pia tangazo, akaliweka juu ya msalaba; na lilikuwa limeandikwa: "Yesu Mnazareti, Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.B: Pilato aliandika pia tangazo, akaagiza liwekwe juu ya msalaba. Maneno yake yalikuwa: "Yesu wa Nazareti, Mfalme wa Wayahudi."
sw.R: Pilato aliandika pia maandishi kwenye kibao, akaagiza kiwekwe juu ya msalaba. Kilisema, "Yesu kutoka Nazareti, Mfalme wa Wayahudi."

vi.L: Phi-lát cũng viết một tấm bảng và đặt trên cây thập tự; trên đó có viết: "Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, Vua của người Do Thái."
vi.B: Phi-lát cũng viết một tấm bảng và cho đặt trên cây thập tự. Bảng ấy ghi: "Giê-xu người Na-xa-rét, Vua dân Do Thái."
vi.R: Phi-lát cũng viết một tấm bảng và cho gắn lên cây thập tự. Trên bảng ghi: "Giê-xu, người từ Na-xa-rét, Vua dân Do Thái."

ko.L: 그리고 빌라도는 명패도 써서 십자가 위에 붙였다. 거기에는 "나사렛 사람 예수, 유대인의 왕"이라고 쓰여 있었다.
ko.B: 빌라도는 죄패도 써서 십자가에 붙이게 했다. 거기에는 "나사렛 예수, 유대인의 왕"이라고 쓰여 있었다.
ko.R: 빌라도는 팻말에 글을 써서 십자가에 붙이게 했다. 팻말에는 "나사렛에서 온 예수, 유대인의 왕"이라고 쓰여 있었다.

pt.L: E Pilatos também escreveu um letreiro e [o] pôs sobre a cruz; e estava escrito: "Jesus, o nazareno, o Rei dos judeus."
pt.B: Pilatos também escreveu um letreiro e mandou colocá-lo na cruz. Nele estava escrito: "Jesus de Nazaré, o Rei dos judeus."
pt.R: Pilatos também escreveu uma placa e mandou pregá-la na cruz. Ela dizia: "Jesus de Nazaré, o Rei dos judeus."

decisions.choice: a notice: a placard stating the charge, the Latin titulus
alternatives: an inscription carved on the cross
decisions.reason: The Greek word is the Latin "titulus", a board or placard with writing on it. Roman writers mention a placard naming a condemned person's crime, carried before him or hung on him; here it is fixed to the cross. The charge is the one Jesus was tried for: claiming to be a king (18:33-37; 19:12).

decisions.choice: the Jews: the Jewish nation, in the title of a king
decisions.reason: In "King of the Jews" the word names the people as a nation, as in Pilate's questions (18:33, 39) and the soldiers' mockery (19:3). It is the Roman charge against Jesus, in Pilate's words, and it is kept as written at every level.

decisions.choice: the charge is also true in John's telling: Jesus is the King of Israel
decisions.reason: Pilate meant the notice as the charge, perhaps with scorn for the people (19:15). John has already shown that Jesus is king in a sense Pilate did not grasp (1:49; 12:13-15; 18:36-37), so the notice says more than its writer intended, as Caiaphas's words did (11:50-52).

decisions.choice: Pilate wrote and put: he is responsible for the notice, whether or not his own hand did the work
alternatives: Pilate wrote it with his own hand
decisions.reason: A governor would normally have such a notice made and put up by others, and Greek often says that a person did what he had done. What matters to the story is that the wording is Pilate's, as he insists in 19:22.

decisions.choice: notice (L, B); sign (R); the Nazorean (L); of Nazareth (B); from Nazareth (R)
decisions.reason: "Title" now usually means the name of a book or a rank, so "notice" and "sign" say what the board was. Literal keeps the form of the word for Jesus's home town, which John uses (18:5, 7); Balanced and Readable say what it means.

decisions.choice: letrero (L, B); cartel (R); el Nazoreo (L); de Nazaret (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "título" now means the name of a book or a rank, so "letrero" and "cartel" say what the board was (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the form of the word John uses for Jesus's home town (also 18:5, 7); Balanced and Readable say what it means. "Rey" has a capital as the title, as in 19:3.

decisions.choice: un écriteau (L, B); une pancarte (R); le Nazôréen (L); de Nazareth (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "titre" now means the name of a book or a rank, so "écriteau" says what the board was (meaning decision m1); Readable uses the everyday "pancarte". Literal keeps the form of the word for Jesus's home town that John uses (18:5, 7); Balanced and Readable say what it means. "Roi" is lowercase, as in 18:33.

decisions.choice: tangazo (L, B); kibao (R); Yesu Mnazareti (L), Yesu wa Nazareti (B), Yesu kutoka Nazareti (R)
decisions.reason: The word is a placard stating the charge (meaning decision m1). "Tangazo" (public notice) says what it was for; Readable says "kibao" (a board with writing), the thing readers can picture. "Anwani" and "cheo" (title, rank) would not be understood as a notice. The forms of "of Nazareth" are those of 18:5 and 18:7.

decisions.choice: "Giê-xu" without "Đức" in the wording of Pilate's notice
decisions.reason: The style guide gives "Đức Giê-xu" at every level because a bare name is disrespectful. That is the narrator's voice; the notice is Pilate's charge against a condemned man, and Pilate would not give him the honorific. The narrator keeps "Đức Giê-xu".

The word is a placard naming the charge (meaning decision). Literal says only "a plate with writing"; Balanced uses the established term for a placard of the charge; Readable uses the everyday word for a sign.

decisions.choice: "나사렛 사람 예수" (L); "나사렛 예수" (B); "나사렛에서 온 예수" (R)
decisions.reason: Korean names Jesus by his town; a transliterated title would mean nothing to readers.

decisions.choice: um letreiro (L, B); uma placa (R)
decisions.reason: "Título" in Portuguese is the name of a book or a rank, as in English. "Letreiro" is a board with writing on it, which is what this was (meaning decision m1); Readable says "placa", the everyday word.

source.text: τοῦτον οὖν τὸν τίτλον πολλοὶ ἀνέγνωσαν τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ὅτι ἐγγὺς ἦν ὁ τόπος τῆς πόλεως ὅπου ἐσταυρώθη ὁ Ἰησοῦς· καὶ ἦν γεγραμμένον Ἑβραϊστί, Ῥωμαϊστί, Ἑλληνιστί.

records.literal_gloss: This then the title many read of the Jews, because near was the place of the city where was crucified the Jesus; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, in Greek.

en.L: So many of the Jews read this notice, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, in Greek.
en.B: Many of the Jews of Jerusalem read this notice, since the spot where Jesus was crucified was close to the city. The notice was in Hebrew, Latin and Greek.
en.R: Many Jewish people from Jerusalem read the sign, because the place where Jesus hung on the cross was close to the city. The sign was written in three languages: Hebrew, Latin and Greek.

es.L: Este letrero, pues, lo leyeron muchos de los judíos, porque el lugar donde Jesús fue crucificado estaba cerca de la ciudad; y estaba escrito en hebreo, en latín, en griego.
es.B: Muchos judíos de Jerusalén leyeron este letrero, porque el sitio donde crucificaron a Jesús estaba cerca de la ciudad. El letrero estaba en hebreo, latín y griego.
es.R: Mucha gente judía de Jerusalén leyó el cartel, porque el lugar donde Jesús estaba en la cruz quedaba cerca de la ciudad. El cartel estaba escrito en tres idiomas: hebreo, latín y griego.

fr.L: Cet écriteau, donc, beaucoup de Juifs le lurent, parce que le lieu où Jésus fut crucifié était près de la ville ; et il était écrit en hébreu, en latin, en grec.
fr.B: Beaucoup de Juifs de Jérusalem lurent cet écriteau, car l’endroit où Jésus avait été crucifié était proche de la ville. L’écriteau était en hébreu, en latin et en grec.
fr.R: Beaucoup de Juifs de Jérusalem ont lu la pancarte, parce que l’endroit où Jésus était sur la croix se trouvait près de la ville. La pancarte était écrite en trois langues : en hébreu, en latin et en grec.

sw.L: Basi wengi wa Wayahudi walilisoma tangazo hili, kwa sababu mahali Yesu aliposulubiwa palikuwa karibu na mji; nalo lilikuwa limeandikwa kwa Kiebrania, kwa Kilatini, kwa Kigiriki.
sw.B: Wayahudi wengi wa Yerusalemu walilisoma tangazo hilo, kwa kuwa mahali Yesu aliposulubiwa palikuwa karibu na mji. Tangazo hilo lilikuwa limeandikwa kwa Kiebrania, Kilatini na Kigiriki.
sw.R: Watu wengi wa Kiyahudi kutoka Yerusalemu walikisoma kibao hicho, kwa sababu mahali Yesu alipotundikwa msalabani palikuwa karibu na mji. Kibao kiliandikwa kwa lugha tatu: Kiebrania, Kilatini na Kigiriki.

vi.L: Vậy nhiều người Do Thái đọc tấm bảng này, vì nơi Đức Giê-xu bị đóng đinh ở gần thành; và bảng ấy được viết bằng tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ, tiếng La-tinh, tiếng Hy Lạp.
vi.B: Nhiều người Do Thái ở Giê-ru-sa-lem đã đọc tấm bảng này, vì nơi Đức Giê-xu bị đóng đinh ở gần thành. Bảng ấy viết bằng tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ, tiếng La-tinh và tiếng Hy Lạp.
vi.R: Nhiều người Do Thái ở Giê-ru-sa-lem đọc tấm bảng ấy, vì nơi Đức Giê-xu bị treo trên cây thập tự ở gần thành. Bảng được viết bằng ba thứ tiếng: tiếng Hê-bơ-rơ, tiếng La-tinh và tiếng Hy Lạp.

ko.L: 그래서 유대인들 가운데 많은 사람이 이 명패를 읽었다. 예수께서 십자가에 못 박히신 곳이 도성에서 가까웠기 때문이다. 그리고 그것은 히브리 말, 라틴 말, 그리스 말로 쓰여 있었다.
ko.B: 예루살렘의 많은 유대인이 이 죄패를 읽었다. 예수께서 십자가에 못 박히신 곳이 도성에서 가까웠기 때문이다. 죄패는 히브리 말과 라틴 말과 그리스 말로 쓰여 있었다.
ko.R: 예루살렘의 많은 유대 사람들이 그 팻말을 읽었다. 예수께서 십자가에 달리신 곳이 성에서 가까웠기 때문이다. 팻말은 히브리 말, 라틴 말, 그리스 말, 이렇게 세 가지 말로 쓰여 있었다.

pt.L: Muitos dos judeus, então, leram este letreiro, porque o lugar onde Jesus foi crucificado ficava perto da cidade; e estava escrito em hebraico, em latim, em grego.
pt.B: Muitos dos judeus de Jerusalém leram esse letreiro, pois o lugar onde Jesus foi crucificado ficava perto da cidade. O letreiro estava em hebraico, latim e grego.
pt.R: Muitos judeus de Jerusalém leram a placa, porque o lugar onde Jesus estava pregado na cruz ficava perto da cidade. A placa estava escrita em três línguas: hebraico, latim e grego.

decisions.choice: the Jews: people of Jerusalem and the festival crowds who passed by
decisions.reason: Here the word means ordinary people who saw the notice because the place was near the city, at Passover when Jerusalem was full of pilgrims. The authorities appear separately in the next sentence as "the chief priests of the Jews".

decisions.choice: near the city: outside the walls, where many people would pass
decisions.reason: Executions took place outside the city (Leviticus 24:14; Numbers 15:35-36; Hebrews 13:12). The Romans crucified people where many would see them, as a warning, and John notes it to explain why so many read the notice.

decisions.choice: Hebrew, Latin, Greek: the local language, the language of Rome, and the common language of the eastern empire
decisions.reason: "Hebrew" is John's word for the language of the Jews of the land, mostly Aramaic in daily speech (19:17). The second word is literally "in Roman", meaning Latin, the language of the Roman government. Greek was spoken across the eastern Mediterranean. In all three languages the notice could be read by everyone in the city at the festival.

decisions.choice: Hebrew, Latin, Greek (SBLGNT)
alternatives: Hebrew, Greek, Latin (many later manuscripts; the King James Version follows this order)
decisions.reason: The manuscripts list the three languages in different orders. The order Hebrew, Latin, Greek is found in several early manuscripts; many later ones read Hebrew, Greek, Latin. The meaning is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Jews of Jerusalem (B); Jewish people from Jerusalem (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the word John wrote and tie it to the people who were there (meaning decision m1), as in 8:48 and 10:31. "Jerusalem" is the city of this sentence ("near the city").

decisions.choice: muchos judíos de Jerusalén (B); mucha gente judía de Jerusalén (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means ordinary people (meaning decision m1), so no level speaks of leaders; as in English, Balanced and Readable tie them to the city of this sentence.

decisions.choice: les Juifs (L); les Juifs de Jérusalem (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the people of the city and the festival crowds, not the authorities (meaning decision m1), so every level keeps "Juifs", which is the French book-wide choice where the people are meant; Balanced and Readable tie it to the city of the sentence, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Wayahudi (L); Wayahudi wa Yerusalemu (B); watu wa Kiyahudi kutoka Yerusalemu (R)
decisions.reason: As the book-wide choice for John: here the word means ordinary people of Jerusalem and the festival crowds (meaning decision m1), so no level says "viongozi" (leaders); the authorities are named separately in the next sentence as "wakuu wa makuhani wa Wayahudi". In "Mfalme wa Wayahudi" (19:19, 21) the word names the nation and is kept at every level.

source.text: ἔλεγον οὖν τῷ Πιλάτῳ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς τῶν Ἰουδαίων· Μὴ γράφε· Ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἀλλ’ ὅτι ἐκεῖνος εἶπεν Βασιλεὺς τῶν Ἰουδαίων εἰμί.

records.literal_gloss: Were saying then to the Pilate the chief priests of the Jews: Not write: The king of the Jews, but that that one said: King of the Jews I am.

en.L: So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, "Do not write, 'The King of the Jews,' but that that man said, 'I am King of the Jews.'"
en.B: The chief priests of the Jews objected. "Do not write 'The King of the Jews,'" they told Pilate. "Write that this man said, 'I am King of the Jews.'"
en.R: So the chief priests of the Jews kept telling Pilate, "Do not write 'The King of the Jews.' Write that this man claimed to be King of the Jews."

es.L: Decían, pues, a Pilato los principales sacerdotes de los judíos: «No escribas: “El Rey de los judíos”, sino que aquel dijo: “Soy Rey de los judíos”».
es.B: Los jefes de los sacerdotes judíos protestaron. «No escribas “El Rey de los judíos”», le dijeron a Pilato. «Escribe que este hombre dijo: “Soy Rey de los judíos”».
es.R: Entonces los jefes de los sacerdotes judíos le insistían a Pilato: «No escribas “El Rey de los judíos”. Escribe que este hombre afirmaba ser el Rey de los judíos».

fr.L: Les chefs des prêtres des Juifs disaient donc à Pilate : « N’écris pas : “Le roi des Juifs”, mais que celui-là a dit : “Je suis roi des Juifs.” »
fr.B: Les chefs des prêtres des Juifs protestèrent. « N’écris pas : “Le roi des Juifs” », dirent-ils à Pilate. « Écris que cet homme a dit : “Je suis roi des Juifs.” »
fr.R: Alors les chefs des prêtres des Juifs répétaient à Pilate : « N’écris pas “Le roi des Juifs”. Écris que cet homme a prétendu être le roi des Juifs. »

sw.L: Basi wakuu wa makuhani wa Wayahudi walikuwa wakimwambia Pilato, "Usiandike, 'Mfalme wa Wayahudi,' bali kwamba yule alisema, 'Mimi ni Mfalme wa Wayahudi.'"
sw.B: Wakuu wa makuhani wa Wayahudi walipinga. "Usiandike, 'Mfalme wa Wayahudi,'" wakamwambia Pilato. "Andika kwamba mtu huyu alisema, 'Mimi ni Mfalme wa Wayahudi.'"
sw.R: Basi viongozi wa makuhani wa Wayahudi waliendelea kumwambia Pilato, "Usiandike 'Mfalme wa Wayahudi.' Andika kwamba mtu huyu alidai kuwa Mfalme wa Wayahudi."

vi.L: Vậy các thầy tế lễ cả của người Do Thái nói với Phi-lát: "Đừng viết: 'Vua của người Do Thái,' mà [viết] rằng người ấy đã nói: 'Tôi là Vua của người Do Thái.'"
vi.B: Các thầy tế lễ cả của người Do Thái phản đối. "Xin đừng viết 'Vua dân Do Thái'," họ nói với Phi-lát. "Hãy viết rằng người này đã nói: 'Tôi là Vua dân Do Thái.'"
vi.R: Vì vậy các thầy tế lễ cả của người Do Thái cứ nói với Phi-lát: "Xin quan đừng viết 'Vua dân Do Thái'. Hãy viết rằng người này tự xưng là Vua dân Do Thái."

ko.L: 그래서 유대인들의 대제사장들이 빌라도에게 거듭 말했다. "'유대인의 왕'이라고 쓰지 마시고, 그 사람이 '나는 유대인의 왕이다'라고 말했다고 [쓰십시오]."
ko.B: 유대인의 대제사장들이 빌라도에게 따졌다. "'유대인의 왕'이라고 쓰지 마시고, 그 사람이 '나는 유대인의 왕이다' 하고 말했다고 쓰십시오."
ko.R: 그래서 유대인의 대제사장들이 빌라도에게 자꾸 말했다. "'유대인의 왕'이라고 쓰지 마십시오. 저 사람이 자기가 유대인의 왕이라고 주장했다고 쓰십시오."

pt.L: Diziam, então, a Pilatos os chefes dos sacerdotes dos judeus: "Não escreva: 'O Rei dos judeus', mas que aquele [homem] disse: 'Sou Rei dos judeus.'"
pt.B: Os chefes dos sacerdotes dos judeus protestaram. "Não escreva 'O Rei dos judeus'", disseram a Pilatos. "Escreva que esse homem disse: 'Eu sou o Rei dos judeus.'"
pt.R: Por isso os chefes dos sacerdotes dos judeus ficavam dizendo a Pilatos: "Não escreva 'O Rei dos judeus'. Escreva que esse homem afirmou ser o Rei dos judeus."

decisions.choice: the chief priests of the Jews: the leading priests in Jerusalem, as heads of the nation
alternatives: the Jewish people as a whole
decisions.reason: Only here does John call them "the chief priests of the Jews". The phrase sets their title beside the one on the cross: the nation's chief priests object to the nation's king. It names the group that objected, the leading priests (18:35; 19:6, 15), not the people.

decisions.choice: were saying ... do not write: an objection pressed more than once, asking Pilate to change what he had put up
alternatives: a request made before the notice was written
decisions.reason: The verb of saying is in a tense that can describe a continuing or repeated action. The command "do not write" is in the present tense: Pilate had already written it (19:19), so they want the wording changed.

decisions.choice: that man said, 'I am King of the Jews': they want the title shown as his claim, not as fact
decisions.reason: The word for "that man" keeps Jesus at a distance, with contempt. As written, the notice states that he is the king; with their change it would only report his claim.

decisions.choice: objected ... they told Pilate (B); kept telling (R); Write that this man ... (B); claimed to be (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show the continuing objection with a verb English uses for it (meaning decision m2), and break the request into two sentences. Readable reports the claim indirectly to avoid quotation marks inside quotation marks.

decisions.choice: los principales sacerdotes de los judíos (L); los jefes de los sacerdotes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The titles as in 19:6. The phrase names the nation's leading priests by their office (meaning decision m1), so it needs no "dirigentes" rendering and no footnote.

decisions.choice: protestaron ... le dijeron (B); le insistían (R); afirmaba ser (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable show the continuing objection with a verb Spanish uses for it (meaning decision m2), and split the request; Readable reports the claim indirectly (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: les chefs des prêtres des Juifs, at every level
decisions.reason: The phrase is heavy in French, but it sets the nation's chief priests beside the nation's king on the notice (meaning decision m1), and "des Juifs" echoes "le roi des Juifs" in the same sentence. "Les chefs des prêtres juifs" would lose that echo.

decisions.choice: celui-là (L); cet homme (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Celui-là" keeps the distance and contempt of the Greek pronoun (meaning decision m3); Balanced and Readable use the plainer "cet homme", as the English does.

decisions.choice: wakuu wa makuhani (L, B); viongozi wa makuhani (R)
decisions.reason: "Wakuu wa makuhani" (Literal, Balanced) and "viongozi wa makuhani" (Readable) for the chief priests, as in chapters 7-12, so the book uses one term.

decisions.choice: "Tôi là Vua ..." in the priests' report of his claim
decisions.reason: The priests put the claim in Jesus's mouth in their own words; they would not give him the "Ta" that the narrative uses when Jesus himself speaks.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη ὁ Πιλᾶτος· Ὃ γέγραφα γέγραφα.

records.literal_gloss: Answered the Pilate: What I have written, I have written.

en.L: Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."
en.B: Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."
en.R: Pilate answered, "What I have written will stay as I wrote it."

es.L: Respondió Pilato: «Lo que he escrito, he escrito».
es.B: Pilato respondió: «Lo que he escrito, escrito se queda».
es.R: Pilato respondió: «Lo que he escrito se queda tal como lo escribí».

fr.L: Pilate répondit : « Ce que j’ai écrit, je l’ai écrit. »
fr.B: Pilate répondit : « Ce que j’ai écrit, je l’ai écrit. »
fr.R: Pilate a répondu : « Ce que j’ai écrit restera comme je l’ai écrit. »

vi.L: Phi-lát trả lời: "Điều tôi đã viết, tôi đã viết."
vi.B: Phi-lát đáp: "Những gì tôi đã viết là đã viết rồi."
vi.R: Phi-lát trả lời: "Tôi đã viết thế nào thì cứ để y như vậy."

ko.L: 빌라도가 대답했다. "내가 쓴 것은 내가 쓴 것이다."
ko.B: 빌라도가 대답했다. "내가 쓴 것은 쓴 그대로 둔다."
ko.R: 빌라도가 대답했다. "내가 쓴 것은 고치지 않겠다."

pt.R: Pilatos respondeu: "O que eu escrevi vai ficar como está."

decisions.choice: What I have written, I have written: it stands and will not be changed
decisions.reason: Greek uses this tense for an action that is done and whose result remains. Saying it twice makes the answer final.

decisions.choice: Pilate's refusal: the governor will not let the priests change his notice
alternatives: Pilate refuses because he believes Jesus is a king
decisions.reason: John does not give Pilate's reason. The priests had just forced his hand (19:12-16), and the notice is a way of answering them. Pilate, who gave way on the sentence, does not give way on the wording, so the title stands over the cross.

decisions.choice: What I have written will stay as I wrote it (R)
alternatives: What I have written, I have written
decisions.reason: Readers new to the Bible may not hear a refusal in the repeated phrase, so Readable says what it means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: escrito se queda (B); se queda tal como lo escribí (R)
alternatives: Lo que he escrito, he escrito (Literal)
decisions.reason: The tense means a thing done whose result stands, and the repetition makes the answer final (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps the repeated verb; Balanced and Readable say plainly that the notice will not be changed.

source.text: οἱ οὖν στρατιῶται ὅτε ἐσταύρωσαν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ἔλαβον τὰ ἱμάτια αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐποίησαν τέσσαρα μέρη, ἑκάστῳ στρατιώτῃ μέρος, καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα.

records.literal_gloss: The then soldiers, when they crucified the Jesus, took the garments of him and made four parts, to each soldier a part, and the tunic.

en.L: Then the soldiers, when they crucified Jesus, took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and [took] the tunic.
en.B: When the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes and divided them into four shares, one share for each soldier. They also took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tunic.
en.R: After the soldiers had nailed Jesus to the cross, they took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes and split them into four parts, one part for each soldier. They also took {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} tunic, the long shirt {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} wore next to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} skin.

es.L: Los soldados, pues, cuando crucificaron a Jesús, tomaron {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ropas e hicieron cuatro partes, una parte para cada soldado, y [tomaron también] la túnica.
es.B: Después de crucificar a Jesús, los soldados tomaron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa y la dividieron en cuatro partes, una para cada soldado. También tomaron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} túnica.
es.R: Después de clavar a Jesús en la cruz, los soldados tomaron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa y la repartieron en cuatro partes, una para cada uno. También tomaron {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} túnica, la camisa larga que llevaba junto a la piel.

fr.L: Les soldats donc, quand ils eurent crucifié Jésus, prirent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements et en firent quatre parts, une part pour chaque soldat, et [ils prirent aussi] la tunique.
fr.B: Quand les soldats eurent crucifié Jésus, ils prirent {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements et les partagèrent en quatre parts, une pour chaque soldat. Ils prirent aussi {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tunique.
fr.R: Après avoir cloué Jésus sur la croix, les soldats ont pris {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements et ils les ont partagés en quatre parts, une pour chaque soldat. Ils ont aussi pris {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} tunique, la longue chemise qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} portait sur la peau.

sw.L: Basi askari, walipomsulubisha Yesu, waliyachukua mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, wakafanya mafungu manne, kila askari fungu moja, na [wakachukua] kanzu pia.
sw.B: Askari walipokwisha kumsulubisha Yesu, walichukua nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, wakazigawa mafungu manne, kila askari fungu lake. Wakachukua pia kanzu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.R: Askari walipokwisha kumpigilia Yesu misumari msalabani, walichukua nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, wakazigawa sehemu nne, kila askari sehemu moja. Wakachukua pia kanzu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, yaani shati refu alilovaa ndani, karibu na ngozi.

vi.L: Vậy khi các binh lính đã đóng đinh Đức Giê-xu, họ lấy áo xống của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chia làm bốn phần, mỗi người lính một phần, và [lấy] cái áo trong.
vi.B: Khi đã đóng đinh Đức Giê-xu, những người lính lấy quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chia làm bốn phần, mỗi người lính một phần. Họ cũng lấy cái áo trong của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Sau khi đóng đinh Đức Giê-xu trên cây thập tự, những người lính lấy quần áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} chia làm bốn phần, mỗi người một phần. Họ cũng lấy cái áo trong của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, là chiếc áo dài {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} mặc sát người.

ko.L: 그래서 병사들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박았을 때, 그분의 겉옷들을 가져다가 네 몫으로 나누어 병사마다 한 몫씩 [가졌고], 속옷도 [가져갔다].
ko.B: 병사들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박은 뒤에 그분의 겉옷을 가져다가 네 몫으로 나누어 한 사람이 한 몫씩 가졌다. 그리고 속에 입는 옷도 가져갔다.
ko.R: 병사들은 예수를 십자가에 못 박은 뒤, 예수의 옷을 가져다가 네 몫으로 나누어 한 사람씩 가졌다. 그리고 예수께서 맨살에 입고 계시던 긴 옷도 가져갔다.

pt.L: Os soldados, então, quando crucificaram Jesus, tomaram as {{deity_pronoun:suas|Suas}} vestes e fizeram quatro partes, uma parte para cada soldado, e [tomaram] a túnica.

decisions.choice: four soldiers: a Roman squad of four carried out the crucifixion
decisions.reason: Roman soldiers often worked in groups of four (compare Acts 12:4). The clothes of a person being executed were usually taken by those who carried out the sentence. The sentence names the Roman soldiers plainly as the ones who crucified Jesus.

decisions.choice: garments: his outer clothing (cloak, belt, sandals and the like); tunic: the long shirt worn next to the skin
alternatives: garments and tunic as two words for the same clothing
decisions.reason: The plural word for garments means outer clothes in general. The tunic was the inner garment, a long shirt reaching to the knees or ankles, worn under the cloak. John sets the tunic apart because of what happens to it next.

decisions.choice: garments (L); clothes (B, R); tunic at every level, explained at Readable
decisions.reason: "Tunic" is the exact word for the long inner shirt; "coat" or "robe" would suggest an outer garment. Readable adds a short description for young readers.

decisions.choice: ropas (L); ropa (B, R); túnica at every level, explained at Readable
decisions.reason: As in English: "túnica" is the exact word for the long inner shirt (meaning decision m2); "manto" would suggest the outer garment. Readable adds a short description.

decisions.choice: ses vêtements; la tunique (every level), explained at Readable
decisions.reason: "Tunique" is the exact French word for the long inner shirt (meaning decision m2); "robe" or "manteau" would suggest an outer garment. French "vêtements" serves every level for the outer clothes. Readable adds a short description for young readers, as the English does.

decisions.choice: kanzu (tunic)
decisions.reason: The tunic was a long shirt reaching to the knees or ankles (meaning decision m2). "Kanzu" is the long one-piece garment Swahili speakers know, so it gives the right picture; "joho" is an outer robe. Readable adds a short description, as the English does, since a kanzu is today often worn as an outer garment.

decisions.choice: "cái áo trong" for the tunic
decisions.reason: "áo dài" today names the Vietnamese national dress, and "áo lót" underwear; "áo trong" says it was the garment worn under the outer clothes. Readable explains it.

decisions.choice: "겉옷들" / "속옷" (L); "겉옷" / "속에 입는 옷" (B); "옷" / "맨살에 입고 계시던 긴 옷" (R)
decisions.reason: The chiton was a long shirt worn next to the skin (meaning decision). Modern "속옷" suggests underwear, so only Literal keeps the short word; Balanced and Readable describe the garment.

decisions.choice: from the top: woven from the top down, in one piece
decisions.reason: John uses the same word elsewhere for "from above" (3:31; 19:11), and "again, from above" (3:3, 7). Here it describes the weaving, from the neck down, with no seam.

decisions.choice: the detail explains why the soldiers did not tear it; John may also see more in it
alternatives: a sign that Jesus is high priest, whose robe was woven without a seam
a picture of the unity of Jesus's people, who are not to be torn apart
decisions.reason: The plain reason for the detail is the next sentence: a seamless tunic was worth more whole. Two further meanings have been proposed. The high priest's robe was to be woven so that it would not tear (Exodus 28:32), and the Jewish historian Josephus says it was not made of two pieces but woven in one. And the word "tear" (19:24) is the word John uses for divisions among people (7:43; 9:16; 10:19) and for the net that was not torn (21:11). John does not say that he means either, so this is uncertain.

decisions.choice: in a single piece from top to bottom (B); in one piece, from the top all the way down (R)
decisions.reason: "Through the whole" means it was woven all in one; Balanced and Readable say so plainly.

decisions.choice: desde arriba
decisions.reason: The same Spanish as "desde arriba" in 19:11, so the reader can see the word John repeats (meaning decision m1); here it describes the weaving. Literal says "toda entera" for "through the whole"; Balanced and Readable say "en una sola pieza".

records.literal_gloss: They said then to one another: Not let us tear it, but let us cast lots for it, whose it will be; so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, the [one] saying: They divided the garments of me among themselves, and for the clothing of me they cast a lot.

en.L: So they said to one another, "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it, [to see] whose it will be," so that the Scripture might be fulfilled which says, "They divided {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garments among themselves, and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothing they cast a lot."
en.B: So they said to each other, "Let us not tear it. Let us cast lots for it and see who gets it." This was so that the Scripture would be fulfilled that says, "They shared out {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} garments among themselves, and for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothing they cast lots."
en.R: So the soldiers said to each other, "Let us not tear it. Let us draw lots to see who will get it." This happened to make the Scripture come true that says, "They divided {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothes among themselves, and they drew lots for {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} clothing."

es.L: Dijeron, pues, entre sí: «No la rasguemos, sino echemos suertes sobre ella, [para ver] de quién será», para que se cumpliera la Escritura que dice: «Se repartieron entre ellos {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ropas, y sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vestidura echaron suerte».
es.B: Así que se dijeron unos a otros: «No la rompamos. Echemos suertes para ver a quién le toca». Esto sucedió para que se cumpliera la Escritura que dice: «Se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ropa entre ellos, y echaron suertes sobre {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vestidura».
es.R: Entonces los soldados se dijeron unos a otros: «No la rompamos. Hagamos un sorteo para ver quién se la queda». Esto sucedió para que se cumpliera lo que dice la Escritura: «Se repartieron {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ropa entre ellos, y sortearon {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} vestidura».

fr.L: Ils se dirent donc les uns aux autres : « Ne la déchirons pas, mais tirons au sort pour elle, [pour savoir] à qui elle sera », afin que s’accomplisse l’Écriture qui dit : « Ils se sont partagé {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} vêtements, et pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} habit ils ont jeté le sort. »
fr.B: Ils se dirent donc entre eux : « Ne la déchirons pas. Tirons-la au sort pour voir à qui elle ira. » C’était pour que s’accomplisse l’Écriture qui dit : « Ils ont partagé entre eux {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} habits, et pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} vêtement ils ont tiré au sort. »
fr.R: Alors les soldats se sont dit entre eux : « Ne la déchirons pas. Tirons au sort pour savoir qui l’aura. » C’est arrivé pour que se réalise ce que dit l’Écriture : « Ils se sont partagé {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} habits, et ils ont tiré au sort pour {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} vêtement. »

sw.L: Basi waliambiana, "Tusiichane, bali tuipigie kura, [tuone] itakuwa ya nani," ili Maandiko yatimie yanayosema, "Waligawanyiana mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} wao kwa wao, na juu ya nguo {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} walitupa kura."
sw.B: Basi waliambiana, "Tusiichane. Tuipigie kura tuone nani atakayeipata." Hili lilikuwa ili Maandiko yatimie yanayosema, "Walijigawia mavazi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, na kwa ajili ya vazi {{deity_pronoun:langu|Langu}} walitupa kura."

vi.L: Vậy họ nói với nhau: "Chúng ta đừng xé nó, nhưng hãy bắt thăm [xem] nó sẽ thuộc về ai," để Kinh Thánh được ứng nghiệm, là lời nói rằng: "Họ đã phân chia áo của tôi cho nhau, và trên y phục của tôi họ đã bắt thăm."
vi.B: Vậy họ bảo nhau: "Đừng xé áo này. Chúng ta hãy bắt thăm xem ai được nó." Việc này xảy ra để ứng nghiệm lời Kinh Thánh: "Họ đem áo của tôi chia cho nhau, và bắt thăm để lấy y phục của tôi."
vi.R: Vậy những người lính bảo nhau: "Đừng xé áo này. Hãy bắt thăm xem ai sẽ được nó." Việc này xảy ra để lời Kinh Thánh trở thành sự thật: "Họ chia quần áo của tôi cho nhau, và bắt thăm để lấy áo của tôi."

ko.L: 그래서 그들이 서로 말했다. "이것을 찢지 말고, 누구의 것이 될지 이것을 두고 제비를 뽑자." 이는 성경이 이루어지게 하려는 것이었으니, [성경은] 이렇게 말한다. "그들이 내 겉옷들을 자기들끼리 나누고, 내 옷을 두고 제비를 뽑았다."
ko.B: 그래서 병사들은 서로 말했다. "이것은 찢지 말고, 제비를 뽑아서 누가 가질지 정하자." 이것은 "그들이 내 겉옷을 서로 나누어 가지고, 내 옷을 두고 제비를 뽑았다" 하는 성경 말씀이 이루어지게 하려는 것이었다.
ko.R: 그래서 병사들은 서로 말했다. "이 옷은 찢지 말자. 제비를 뽑아서 누가 가질지 정하자." 이 일로 성경에 기록된 말씀이 이루어졌다. "그들이 내 옷을 서로 나누어 가지고, 내 옷을 두고 제비를 뽑았다."

pt.L: Disseram, então, uns aos outros: "Não a rasguemos, mas tiremos a sorte sobre ela, [para ver] de quem será", para que se cumprisse a Escritura que diz: "Repartiram entre si as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} vestes, e sobre a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} roupa lançaram sorte."
pt.B: Então disseram uns aos outros: "Não vamos rasgá-la. Vamos tirar a sorte para ver quem fica com ela." Isso aconteceu para que se cumprisse a Escritura que diz: "Repartiram entre si as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} vestes, e sobre a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} roupa lançaram sortes."
pt.R: Por isso os soldados disseram uns aos outros: "Não vamos rasgar a túnica. Vamos fazer um sorteio para ver quem vai ficar com ela." Isso aconteceu para que se cumprisse o que diz a Escritura: "Repartiram entre si as {{deity_pronoun:minhas|Minhas}} roupas e fizeram um sorteio para ver quem ficaria com a {{deity_pronoun:minha|Minha}} túnica."

decisions.choice: cast lots: a game of chance to decide who would have it
decisions.reason: Lots were marked stones or pieces of bone, thrown or drawn to decide a matter. Soldiers also played with dice. Either way, chance decided which soldier kept the tunic whole.

decisions.choice: Psalm 22:19, quoted word for word from the Greek translation of the psalm
decisions.reason: The words are those of Psalm 22:19 in the Greek translation used in John's day, which follows the Hebrew closely. The psalm is the prayer of a righteous sufferer, surrounded by enemies, who is rescued by God; its first line is Jesus's cry in Matthew 27:46 and Mark 15:34. John uses it to show that what the soldiers did was foretold.

decisions.choice: John reads the psalm's two lines as two acts: the garments divided, the tunic given by lot
alternatives: the two lines say one thing twice, as Hebrew poetry often does
decisions.reason: In the psalm the two lines are parallel and describe one act. John's account matches each line to a separate deed: the soldiers divide the outer garments (19:23) and cast lots for the tunic.

decisions.choice: so that the Scripture might be fulfilled: the narrator's comment on God's purpose, not the soldiers' aim
alternatives: the soldiers acted in order to fulfill Scripture
decisions.reason: The soldiers knew nothing of the psalm. John's formula (12:38; 13:18; 15:25; 19:36) says that what happened was in keeping with what God had said beforehand.

decisions.choice: This was so that ... (B); This happened to make ... come true (R)
alternatives: so that the Scripture might be fulfilled (Literal, joined to the soldiers' words)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence for John's comment so that it is not read as part of what the soldiers said (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: draw lots (R); cast lots (L, B)
decisions.reason: "Draw lots" is the plainer phrase for young readers and keeps the sense of chance without naming a game the text does not name.

decisions.choice: Esto sucedió para que ... (B, R)
alternatives: para que se cumpliera la Escritura (Literal, joined to the soldiers' words)
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable start a new sentence for John's comment so that it is not read as part of what the soldiers said (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: hagamos un sorteo; sortearon (R); echar suertes (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday words for deciding by chance, without naming a game the text does not name (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: tirer au sort (every level); jeter le sort (L, in the psalm)
decisions.reason: French "tirer au sort" covers both "cast" and "draw" lots and keeps the sense of chance without naming a game the text does not name (meaning decision m1). In the quotation Literal keeps the psalm's picture of throwing a lot. Balanced and Readable start a new sentence for John's comment so that it is not read as part of the soldiers' words (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: kupigia kura, kutupa kura (L, B); kuamua kwa bahati (R)
decisions.reason: Lots were thrown or drawn to let chance decide (meaning decision m1). "Kura" is the old word for a lot, but today "kupiga kura" usually means to vote, so Readable says "kuamua kwa bahati" (decide by chance). "Kamari" (gambling) would name a game the text does not name. Literal and Balanced say "kutupa kura" (throw lots) in the psalm, keeping its picture.

decisions.choice: "tôi" in the psalm, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The words are the psalmist's lament (Psalm 22), and a Vietnamese lament says "tôi". "Ta" is how Jesus speaks of himself with authority; it would sound wrong in a cry of distress. The English "my" carries a span; "tôi" takes none.

decisions.choice: "제비를 뽑다" for both casting lots in this verse, at every level
decisions.reason: The ordinary Korean phrase for deciding by lot; one phrase lets the reader see that the soldiers do just what the psalm says.

decisions.choice: tirar a sorte, lançar sortes (L, B); fazer um sorteio (R)
decisions.reason: "Tirar a sorte" and "lançar sortes" are the Portuguese phrases for deciding by lot (meaning decision m1). Readable says "fazer um sorteio", the everyday word, and names no game the text does not name.

pt.L: E estavam de pé junto à cruz de Jesus a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe e a irmã da {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe, Maria, a [mulher] de Clopas, e Maria Madalena.
pt.B: Enquanto isso, junto à cruz de Jesus estavam a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe, a irmã dela, Maria, mulher de Clopas, e Maria Madalena.
pt.R: Algumas mulheres estavam de pé perto da cruz de Jesus. Eram a mãe {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, a irmã dela, Maria, a mulher de Clopas, e Maria Madalena.

decisions.choice: four women: his mother, his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene
alternatives: three women: his mother's sister is Mary the wife of Clopas
two women: his mother and her sister, named as the two Marys
decisions.reason: The Greek has no "and" between "his mother's sister" and "Mary of Clopas", so they could be the same woman. But then two sisters would both be called Mary, which is unlikely. Read as four, the list falls into two pairs joined by "and": two women not named, then two named Marys. The evidence is not decisive.

decisions.choice: Mary the wife of Clopas
decisions.reason: The Greek says only "Mary of Clopas", a way of naming a woman by a man she belonged to, most often her husband, sometimes her father or son. "Wife" is the usual sense. Nothing more is known of Clopas; whether he is the Cleopas of Luke 24:18 is uncertain.

decisions.choice: Magdalene: from Magdala, a town on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Mary Magdalene is named here for the first time in John; she is the first to find the tomb empty and to see the risen Jesus (20:1-18). Luke 8:2 says Jesus had freed her from seven demons.

decisions.choice: his mother's sister: John does not name her
decisions.reason: Other Gospels name women at the cross: Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and Salome or the mother of Zebedee's sons (Matthew 27:56; Mark 15:40). Whether John's unnamed sister of Jesus's mother is one of these cannot be known from the text.

decisions.choice: Meanwhile (B); Some women were standing (R)
decisions.reason: The sentence turns from the soldiers to the people who loved Jesus (19:24 meaning decision m1). Balanced marks the turn with "Meanwhile"; Readable starts with the women and then lists them, without saying how many (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: María la de Cleofás (L); María la esposa de Cleofás (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Cleofás" is the form Spanish has long used for this name; it does not settle whether he is the Cleopas of Luke 24:18 (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps "la de", the Spanish way of naming a woman by her husband or family, which matches the Greek; Balanced and Readable say "esposa", the usual sense.

decisions.choice: Mientras tanto (B); Cerca de la cruz de Jesús había unas mujeres (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: the sentence turns from the soldiers to the people who loved Jesus (19:24, meaning decision m1). Readable names the women after saying they were there, without saying how many (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Marie de Magdala
decisions.reason: "Marie-Madeleine" is the traditional French name, but it hides what the Greek word says, that she came from Magdala (meaning decision m3); "Marie de Magdala" says it plainly and is the shared French choice for John. A native reviewer may prefer the traditional form.

decisions.choice: la sœur de sa mère (B, R)
decisions.reason: French "sa sœur" after "sa mère" could mean Jesus's sister, so Balanced and Readable repeat "sa mère"; "sa tante" would be plain but adds a word John does not use.

decisions.choice: dada wa mama yake (B, R)
decisions.reason: In Swahili "dada yake" after "mama yake" could be read as Jesus's own sister, so Balanced and Readable keep the Greek's "his mother's sister" (meaning decision m4).

decisions.choice: "chị em gái"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese kinship words say whether a sister is older or younger ("dì" is usually a mother's younger sister). John does not say, so the neutral "chị em gái" is used.

decisions.choice: "이모" (B, R) for "his mother's sister"; "어머니의 자매" (L)
decisions.reason: Korean has a plain word for a mother's sister; Literal keeps the Greek phrase. "그리고" before the last name helps the reader count four women, as the meaning decision reads them.

source.text: Ἰησοῦς οὖν ἰδὼν τὴν μητέρα καὶ τὸν μαθητὴν παρεστῶτα ὃν ἠγάπα λέγει τῇ μητρί· Γύναι, ἴδε ὁ υἱός σου·

en.B: Jesus saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother there, and near her the disciple whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved. He said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "Woman, look, here is your son."
en.R: Jesus saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother there. The disciple whom {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved was standing near her. Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} mother, "Mother, he is your son now."

es.L: Jesús, pues, viendo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre y al discípulo a quien amaba, que estaba al lado, dice a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Mujer, mira, tu hijo».
es.B: Jesús vio allí a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre, y junto a ella al discípulo a quien amaba. Le dijo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Mujer, mira, este es tu hijo».
es.R: Jesús vio allí a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre. El discípulo a quien Jesús amaba estaba cerca de ella. Entonces le dijo a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} madre: «Madre, desde ahora él es tu hijo».

fr.L: Jésus donc, voyant {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère et, se tenant près [d’elle], le disciple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait, dit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Femme, voici ton fils. »
fr.B: Jésus vit {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère, et près d’elle le disciple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait. Il dit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Femme, voici ton fils. »
fr.R: Jésus a vu {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère. Le disciple qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} aimait se tenait près d’elle. Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} mère : « Mère, c’est ton fils, maintenant. »

sw.L: Basi Yesu, alipomwona mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na yule mwanafunzi ambaye alimpenda akiwa amesimama karibu, anamwambia mama {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, "Mama, tazama, mwana wako."

vi.L: Vậy Đức Giê-xu, thấy mẹ và người môn đồ mà {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu đứng bên cạnh, nói với mẹ: "Thưa bà, kìa, con của bà."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu thấy mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng đó, và gần bà là người môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu. Ngài nói với mẹ: "Thưa mẹ, đây là con của mẹ."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu thấy mẹ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đứng đó. Người môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} yêu đứng gần bà. Đức Giê-xu nói với mẹ: "Mẹ ơi, từ nay người này là con của mẹ."

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 어머니와, 곁에 서 있는 사랑하시는 제자를 보시고, 어머니께 말씀하신다. "여자여, 보세요, 당신의 아들이에요."
ko.B: 예수께서 어머니와, 그 곁에 서 있는 사랑하시는 제자를 보시고 어머니께 말씀하셨다. "어머니, 보세요, 이 사람이 어머니의 아들이에요."
ko.R: 예수께서 어머니를 보셨다. 예수께서 사랑하시는 제자도 그 곁에 서 있었다. 예수께서 어머니께 말씀하셨다. "어머니, 이제 이 사람이 어머니의 아들이에요."

pt.L: Jesus, então, vendo a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe e, ali perto, o discípulo a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} amava, diz à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe: "Mulher, eis o seu filho."
pt.B: Jesus viu ali a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe e, perto dela, o discípulo a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} amava. Ele disse à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe: "Mulher, aqui está o seu filho."
pt.R: Jesus viu a {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe ali. O discípulo a quem {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} amava estava perto dela. Jesus disse à {{deity_pronoun:sua|Sua}} mãe: "Mãe, agora ele é o seu filho."

decisions.choice: Woman: a respectful address, as at Cana
decisions.reason: Jesus uses this address to his mother only twice, at Cana (2:4) and here. At Cana he said, "My hour has not yet come"; now his hour has come (12:23; 13:1; 17:1), and at the cross he speaks to her again in the same way. The address was courteous, not rude.

decisions.choice: look, your son: a declaration that makes a new bond, the disciple to be her son
alternatives: only pointing out the disciple standing there
decisions.reason: The words do not simply point at someone; they give the disciple to her as a son, and the next sentence gives her to him as a mother. The disciple acts on it at once (19:27).

decisions.choice: a dying son's care for his mother; perhaps also the start of a new family of his disciples
alternatives: chiefly a symbol, with the mother standing for a people of faith
decisions.reason: The first sense is plain: Jesus makes sure his mother will be cared for. His brothers did not yet believe in him (7:5). John may also mean more: from the cross Jesus joins his mother and his disciple as one family, and after the resurrection he calls his disciples "my brothers" (20:17). The text does not say so directly.

decisions.choice: the disciple whom Jesus loved: the disciple John does not name
decisions.reason: This disciple first appears at the last supper (13:23) and stands at the cross when the other disciples have scattered (16:32). The Gospel says he is the source of its witness (19:35; 21:24).

decisions.choice: said (B, R); says (L), and so through this passage (19:27, 19:28)
decisions.reason: John often tells past events in the present tense ("he says") for vividness. Literal keeps the present; Balanced and Readable use the past, as English normally tells a story. This applies to every such verb in this passage.

decisions.choice: Woman
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "Woman" so that readers can connect this scene with Cana (2:4); the footnote on meaning decision m1 says the address was respectful. "Dear woman" would add warmth the word does not carry on its own.

decisions.choice: Mother, he is your son now (R)
decisions.reason: For young readers "Woman" sounds rude, which the Greek is not. She is his mother, so Readable uses the address a son would use, as it does at 2:4. "Now" shows that the words make a new bond (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Mujer (L, B); Madre (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the address is respectful (meaning decision m1), though "mujer" on its own can sound cold. Literal and Balanced keep it so that readers can link the cross with Cana; the footnote says it was courteous. Readable says "Madre", the address a son would use, and "desde ahora" shows that the words make a new bond (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: mira, tu hijo (L); mira, este es tu hijo (B)
decisions.reason: The word calls attention and gives the disciple to her as a son (meaning decision m2). "He ahí" is a familiar but dated form. Verse 27 uses the same wording for "tu madre". "Él" in Readable is the disciple and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: Femme (L, B); Mère (R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: Literal and Balanced keep "Femme" so that readers can connect the cross with Cana; the address was respectful (meaning decision m1). For young readers "Femme" sounds cold, so Readable uses the address a son would use, and "maintenant" shows that the words make a new bond (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Mama at every level
decisions.reason: The address is respectful in Greek (meaning decision m1). Calling a woman "Mwanamke!" to her face is rude in Swahili, so even Literal cannot keep the word without changing the tone. "Mama" is the respectful address to an older woman, and it also names her as his mother. It is the word used at Cana (2:4), so the link between the two scenes is kept.

decisions.choice: "Thưa bà" (L); "Thưa mẹ" (B); "Mẹ ơi" (R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide: Literal keeps the Greek "Woman" as a respectful "Thưa bà"; in Balanced and Readable a son speaking to his mother says "mẹ", since "bà" from a son would sound cold, which the Greek is not.

decisions.choice: "nói" with no past marker (L), "nói" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's historic present here and in 19:27-28 by leaving out "đã". "Nói" is the book's verb for Jesus speaking (docs/vietnamese-style.md).

decisions.choice: "여자여" (L); "어머니" (B, R)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the Greek address is respectful, but "여자여" said to one's own mother sounds cold in Korean. Literal keeps the word John wrote; Balanced and Readable say "어머니". The English keeps "Woman" at Balanced, so the Korean differs there.

decisions.choice: Jesus speaks to his mother in the polite style (해요체: "보세요", "아들이에요"), and to the disciple in the plain style (19:27)
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: the plain style would be disrespectful from a son to his mother in Korean. Literal keeps "당신" for the Greek pronoun, as at 2:4.

decisions.choice: historic present "말씀하신다" (L); past (B, R), in 19:26-28
decisions.reason: Literal keeps John's present tense in narrative; Balanced and Readable tell the story in the past. One decision for 19:17-30.

decisions.choice: Mulher (L, B), Mãe (R), with "você" forms: o seu filho; a sua mãe (19:27)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to people with "você" (style section 4), his mother and the disciple included, so the possessive is "seu"; "teu" would bring in the archaic register of older Bibles. "Mulher" at Literal and Balanced keeps the link with Cana (2:4), as the English does; Readable says "Mãe".

source.text: εἶτα λέγει τῷ μαθητῇ· Ἴδε ἡ μήτηρ σου.

pt.B: Depois disse ao discípulo: "Aqui está a sua mãe."
pt.R: Depois disse ao discípulo: "Agora ela é a sua mãe."

decisions.choice: look, your mother: the other half of the declaration in 19:26
decisions.reason: The two sayings match: she is to be his mother, and he is to be her son. Together they put her in the disciple's care as a son cares for his mother.

decisions.choice: She is your mother now (R)
decisions.reason: As in 19:26, Readable says what the words do, giving the disciple a mother to care for.

decisions.choice: Desde ahora ella es tu madre (R)
decisions.reason: As in 19:26, Readable says what the words do: they give the disciple a mother to care for (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: Jesus to the disciple: "con"
decisions.reason: As the style guide: Jesus speaks to a disciple as "con". It also suits the new family bond he is making.

es.R: A partir de ese momento, aquel discípulo se la llevó a vivir a su casa.

vi.B: Từ lúc đó, người môn đồ ấy đón bà về nhà mình.
